thread:
sam: Heads-up: after the 6.4 roll (eu-west2 nodes), we're seeing a spike in hosts failing to bring up the GPU driver. ~30% of p4s report driver probe errors and a handful of OOMs.
lia: Ugh. Can you paste the dmesg snippet?
sam: paste: `nvidia: probe of 0000:0a:00.0 failed with error -22` and `NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:0a:00): 31, pid=1223, name=python`
miguel: That looks like the kernel changed PCI resource handling. Any DKMS rebuilds?
sam: DKMS shows modules built but `modinfo nvidia` returns different vermagic. DKMS output: ```
$ dkms status
-nvidia/525.89.02, 6.4.0, x86_64: installed
````
jen: Sounds like vermagic mismatch to me. Did initramfs get regenerated after the kernel image was installed?
sam: Not on all hosts; some were live-upgraded during rolling deploy. Those are the ones failing.
lia: Immediate actions: 1) cordon affected hosts 2) drain pods/evacuate workloads 3) shift provisioning to us-central1 as capacity buffer 4) open rollback plan for the 6.4 kernel image.
miguel: I'll script a mass `apt-get install --reinstall linux-image-6.3` fallback and add a taint label for nodes that didn't regenerate initramfs.
infra-bot: [alert] Capacity pressure increased in eu-west2; 12 pods pending for GPU class for last 18m
jen: We should also check NCCL errors in the GKE logs — if probes failed during CUDA init we might be seeing silent collective timeouts.
sam: Found NCCL warn: `NET/Plugin : Bind error - Address already in use` on the failing hosts. Could be socket namespace changes in 6.4.
lia: If it's socket namespace or binder semantics, rolling back is safer than chasing kernel patches. Can we cut a canary rollback to 10 hosts and validate?
miguel: Yes. I'll pick 10 hosts in eu-west2 with low utilization and rollback overnight. I'll also add a check: `modprobe nvidia || dmesg | tail -n 40` and collect outputs.
jen: Ops note — rolling back will temporarily reduce available capacity. We should advertise reduced SLA to internal customers and trigger the escalations page.
sam: For immediate mitigation I've put a temporary autoscaling policy to favor dedicated pools in us-central1 and disabled auto-upgrade for the rest of the eu-west2 pool.
lia: Post-mortem items: - enforce initramfs regeneration in kernel upgrade playbook - add `vermagic` check to node-provisioning CI - add a canary group for kernel+driver compatibility before broad rollout
miguel: Also file bug with distro: indicate `PCI resource assignment changed causing nvidia probe -22` and attach dmesg + `modinfo` outputs.
jen: Who's owning the rollback?
miguel: Taking it. Will update this thread with progress and timestamps.
sam: Thanks. If anyone sees additional `Xid` patterns or host reboots, ping me. :pray:
infra-bot: [action] created ticket INF-3271: kernel-6.4-eu-west2-driver-probe-failures (assigned: miguel)
lia: Good. After rollback, let's run a small synthetic workload (BERT perf) to validate latency + NCCL stability before uncordoning.
sam: Agreed. I'll coordinate the validation run and collect perf traces.
jen: Thx team. Keep messages short in here so oncall can triage easily.
miguel: starting rollback now on 10 canary hosts (eu-west2-a). ETA ~2h.
jen: noted.
(small follow-up after 1h)
miguel: Canary rollback complete on 10 hosts, `modprobe nvidia` OK, NCCL init passes, pending validation. Turning on drain for remaining failing hosts in batches.
sam: Seeing reduced pending pods in eu-west2, queue length down from 18 to 3.
lia: Great. Once validated, we can stage a wider rollback and gate upgrades until vermagic/initramfs step is explicit in pipeline. :white_check_mark:
